nodes.label: Operations Runbook
nodes.rationale: How to run it, how to verify it works, and what every failure actually hit here means. Written for whoever picks this up next.

nodes.label: Local Startup: Four Processes
nodes.rationale: npm run db start then npm run dev brings up the API on :3000 and three Vite servers on :5173 (member), :5175 (admin) and :5176 (outlet), sharing one database. Allow about 20 seconds — an earlier check at 15s reported the API down when it was still starting.

nodes.label: Request Flow End to End
nodes.rationale: Nobody approves anything: a guest is entitled to every published benefit the moment they join, so a request is a notice telling one outlet to expect them. Three rules worth exercising — announce twice in a minute (429, and still refused after an API restart because the throttle counts rows), confirm the same notice twice (already_closed), and look for another outlet's notice (404, not 403).

nodes.label: Card Scan End to End
nodes.rationale: For a guest who never opens the app, which is the whole point of the card back. Entitlements appear filtered to what this outlet can honour. Worth trying: scan then wait ten minutes before recording (refused, the verification session expired) and scan on one outlet screen then record from another (refused, the session is bound to the account that made it).

nodes.label: Managing Outlet Devices
nodes.rationale: One row per physical device, not one shared token per outlet. Copy the plaintext from the one-time panel immediately — the API stores only a SHA-256 digest. Rotation and revocation increment tokenVersion and revoke the refresh family so an open session dies rather than lasting out its access token. A blank Last used means provisioned but never signed in.

nodes.label: Six Verification Layers
nodes.rationale: Database reachable, schema current, types sound, tests pass, server boots, end to end. A failure at layer n makes the layers above it meaningless. Layer 5 matters on its own: the test suite builds the app in-process, so it can pass while npm run dev fails — startup-only faults like a missing env var, plugin ordering or the R17 boot check surface only there.

nodes.label: Known Failure Modes
nodes.rationale: Every one has actually happened here: PowerShell execution policy, .env not loading outside apps/api, npm swallowing a leading -- before a script flag, EPERM renaming the Prisma engine DLL while the API holds it, a UTF-8 BOM from Out-File breaking a migration, non-ASCII characters killing a .ps1, PowerShell mangling case-sensitive table quoting, and suite-only failures from shared in-memory state.

nodes.label: TOTP Replay Guard Looks Like Flakiness
nodes.rationale: StaffUser.mfaLastUsedEpoch refuses a code at or before the last used period even when cryptographically valid, which is what stops one observed over a shoulder being replayed. It surfaces as acceptance-journey.test.ts failing 401 at step 1 when the seeded administrator signs in twice inside the same 30-second window — precisely what you do when investigating a failure. Wait half a minute; do not weaken the replay check.

nodes.label: Traps That Do Not Announce Themselves
nodes.rationale: The dangerous class: things that pass every test while being wrong. Spreading a scope fragment, money through a float, a benefit value creeping into code, and 403 where 404 is required.

nodes.label: What Is Not Covered by Tests
nodes.rationale: Stated so nobody mistakes a green suite for completeness: secrets are environment variables rather than a KMS, rate limiting is in-memory and resets on restart, and Docker is unverified because it is not installed on the development machine.

nodes.label: npm run mfa:code Development Helper
nodes.rationale: Reads the account's stored secret, decrypts it and prints a fresh code every 30 seconds. Deliberately not an echo inside the sign-in path — a TOTP code is a function of the clock, so a code printed at sign-in would expire while you read it and the replay check would refuse the retry. Exits unless NODE_ENV=development, and being a script nobody invokes it cannot be left switched on the way a flag can.
